summary.key_finding: All 5/5 hardware epochs show negative η. All 4 powered epochs (SNR ≥ 1.5σ) show negative η. The probability that this sign consistency arises by chance (random sign per epoch) is ≤ 0.0312. This is strong evidence that the observed modulation is tied to the gravitational geometry (Earth-Moon-Sun orientation), not to hardware-specific instrumental systematics which would produce random sign variations across independent hardware eras.
summary.systematic_discrimination: Sign consistency across independent hardware epochs rules out instrumental systematics. Chi2 percentile 100% indicates epoch-varying noise, not sign-reversing artifacts.

chi2_noise_analysis.interpretation: Observed chi2/dof = 4.3. Under the hypothesis of a constant eta = -3.17e-04 with epoch-varying noise, simulated chi2/dof has median = 0.8 and 95th percentile = 2.3. The observed chi2/dof is at the 100th percentile of the expected distribution under heteroscedastic noise — above the 95th percentile, suggesting additional variance beyond noise.

amplitude_rms_correlation.interpretation: Amplitude scatter positively correlates with per-epoch RMS — consistent with noise-driven variation (not a systematic artifact).
